newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-WEATHER IMPROVES FOR NZ-SRI LANKA MATCH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEATHER IMPROVES FOR NZ-SRI LANKA MATCH.

text.p: Improving weather conditions have raised hopes that play in Sunday's one-day international between Sri Lanka and New Zealand at Eden Park can begin around 1.30 p.m. (0130 GMT).
The match, the first in a three-game series, was originally scheduled for Saturday but was postponed because of heavy rain. The start time was again delayed on Sunday morning due to rain.
However, commentators said the skies had cleared and the covers had come off the pitch.
The forecast is for cloudy weather with fine periods but with showers expected through the day.
Given there has to be enough time for both teams to receive a minimum of 25 overs, 2.00 p.m. (0200 GMT) is the latest play could get underway.
